title: Lines of symmetry
goal: I can find lines of symmetry in shapes, letters and pictures.
teach: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that are mirror images. If you fold the shape on the line, the halves fit exactly. A square has 4 lines of symmetry. A rectangle has 2. Some shapes have none.

ex.q: How many lines of symmetry does the letter H have?
steps: Test a vertical line through the middle: the left and right halves match.
Test a horizontal line through the middle: the top and bottom halves match.

watch: A rectangle’s diagonal is not a line of symmetry: if you fold on it, the halves do not fit.

qs.text: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle (3 equal sides) have?
qs.hint: One line from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
qs.steps:
1. Rule: a line of symmetry folds a shape into two halves that fit exactly on top of each other (mirror images).
2. A line from each corner to the middle of the opposite side folds the triangle into matching halves.
3. There are 3 corners, so there are 3 lines of symmetry.

qs.text: How many lines of symmetry does the letter E have?
qs.steps:
1. Rule: a line of symmetry folds a shape into two halves that fit exactly on top of each other (mirror images).
2. A horizontal line through the middle arm: the top and bottom halves match.
3. A vertical line: the halves do not match.
4. E has 1 line of symmetry.

qs.text: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon (6 equal sides) have?
qs.hint: 3 lines through opposite corners, 3 through the middles of opposite sides.
qs.steps:
1. Rule: a line of symmetry folds a shape into two halves that fit exactly on top of each other (mirror images).
2. Lines through opposite corners: 6 corners ÷ 2 = 3 lines.
3. Lines through the middles of opposite sides: 6 sides ÷ 2 = 3 lines.
4. 3 + 3 = 6 lines of symmetry.
